themes_detail.label: Street Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints spiked to 49 THIS WEEK, up 273% from the 8-week baseline of 13.1 per week (z-score: 8.8), signaling a newly accelerated disruption pattern affecting outdoor quality of life in Elmhurst/South Corona.
evidence: 49 street/sidewalk noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 13.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (273% spike, z-score 8.8)
Concurrent commercial noise complaints at 22 two weeks ago (193% above 7.5 baseline, z-score 4.59), suggesting multi-source noise escalation
Mobile food vendor complaints also spiked to 4 THIS WEEK (700% above 0.5 baseline), potentially indicating outdoor commercial activity as noise driver
reporting_angles: Interview residents on specific streets experiencing the noise surge; identify whether it's construction, vendor activity, or changed enforcement patterns
Map the 49 complaints geographically to identify hotspots and interview affected block associations or community leaders

themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints jumped to 4 THIS WEEK, a 700% increase from the 0.5 weekly average (z-score: 7.0), suggesting either a sudden surge in unpermitted vending or a new community enforcement response in this week.
evidence: 4 mobile food vendor complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average over 8 weeks (700% spike, z-score 7.0)
Timing coincides with street noise spike (49 complaints THIS WEEK), suggesting outdoor commercial activity as a driver
Street sign missing complaints also at 4 THIS WEEK (700% above baseline), indicating possible infrastructure or vendor-related activity
reporting_angles: Determine whether the spike reflects actual increase in unpermitted vendors or changed community reporting behavior
Interview street vendors and local business associations about licensing, enforcement, and any recent policy changes

themes_detail.label: Elevator Outages Surge
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints jumped to 27 LAST WEEK, up 266% from the 7.4 weekly baseline (z-score: 6.46), indicating a sudden spike in building infrastructure failures affecting multi-unit residents across the district.
evidence: 27 elevator complaints LAST WEEK vs. 7.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (266% spike, z-score 6.46)
Concurrent spike in plumbing complaints (278 over 90 days) and residential disposal complaints (5 last week, 400% above 1.0 baseline) suggests building-wide infrastructure stress
Heat/hot water remains top complaint category (2021 over 90 days), indicating broader building maintenance issues across the district
reporting_angles: Report on which buildings or building types are experiencing elevator failures; interview residents in affected buildings
Investigate whether DOB has received permit filings for elevator repairs or whether landlords are deferring maintenance

themes_detail.label: Special Projects Inspection Team (SPIT) Alert
themes_detail.summary: SPIT complaints spiked to 5 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 1900% increase from the 0.2 baseline (z-score: 10.97, highest recorded spike), suggesting a major enforcement action or inspection campaign was triggered in the district.
evidence: 5 SPIT complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1900% spike, z-score 10.97—highest anomaly in dataset)
SPIT is a Sanitation enforcement unit; spike timing precedes concurrent curb condition spike (5 complaints TWO WEEKS AGO, 567% above baseline, z-score 9.81)
Pattern suggests enforcement action or environmental compliance sweep occurred in the district
reporting_angles: Contact DSNY and SPIT for incident reports; determine what triggered the inspection campaign and which locations were targeted
Cross-reference with curb condition complaints and drug activity reports to determine whether enforcement was environmental, compliance-focused, or multi-agency

themes_detail.label: Curb & Street Infrastructure Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Curb condition complaints spiked to 5 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 567% increase from 0.8 baseline (z-score: 9.81), alongside street sign missing complaints at 4 THIS WEEK (700% above baseline), indicating accelerating street infrastructure neglect.
evidence: Curb condition complaints at 5 TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 0.8 weekly average (567% spike, z-score 9.81)
Street sign missing complaints at 4 THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average (700% spike, z-score 4.95)
Street condition complaints remain high at 679 over 90 days; combined with recent spikes, suggests maintenance backlog is worsening
reporting_angles: Photograph and map the affected curb and street sign locations; interview DOT about maintenance scheduling and budget constraints
Determine whether these complaints correlate with recent construction (5 DOB filings in 90 days) or deferred maintenance cycles
